title: Connect jump leads in the safe order
instruction: Connect the jump leads to jump-start the dead battery.
context: UK HSE guide INDG139: "Many explosions happen when batteries are being connected or disconnected." Its jump-start order: red lead "to the non-earthed terminal of the flat battery", then black lead "to a suitable unpainted metal part of the chassis or engine of the dead vehicle. The point of attachment should be at least 15 cm from the battery". O*NET 53-6031.00: "Test and charge batteries."
setup: Station table; cm from the midpoint between the arm bases on the table (x forward, y left). Donor battery: blue box 12x20x12 cm at x 64, y 3, with two decorative posts on top (cylinders 18 mm dia, 20 mm tall, red at x 62, y 8 and black at x 62, y -2; the leads do not attach to them). Jump leads: 8 mm PVC, 38 cm, red at y 6 and black at y 0, fixed to the table at x 57.4, lying straight towards the robot; each ends in a 40x20x16 mm 20 g clamp block (red / black) centred at x 17.4. Dead battery: dark grey box 14x18x5 cm at x 40, y 22. On its top two pads at x 40: red + pad at y 26.5, black - pad at y 17.5. Engine block: dark grey box 8x8x4 cm at x 36, y -10, with a silver bare-metal ground pad on top. Each pad: 60x60 mm recess, 2 mm plate inside 4 mm walls 8 mm tall, all in the pad colour.
scoring: Measured with a ruler at the end, plus watching the trial for the order. The safe order is: red clamp into the dead battery's red + pad first, then the black clamp into the silver ground pad on the engine block, never onto the battery. Score 0 if at any time during the trial: the black clamp touches the ground pad while the red clamp is not seated in the + pad (wrong order: black connected first, or red taken off while black is connected), which scores 0 even if both clamps end up in the right pads; the black clamp touches the battery's - pad or the + pad; or the red clamp touches the - pad or the ground pad (touched = clamp centre within 1.5 cm of the pad's walls, no higher than a clamp lying on top of the walls plus 4 mm). Any of these counts for the whole trial: moving the clamp to the right pad afterwards does not undo it. Score 0 if at the end either gripper still holds or touches a clamp (released = both gripper centres, between the finger pads, at least 3 cm from both clamps). Otherwise +0.5 for the red clamp seated in the + pad (centre over the 60x60 mm recess floor and at most 16 mm above the plate, i.e. lying down in it, not on the walls) and +0.5 for the black clamp seated in the ground pad. Nothing connected = 0; red only, released = 0.5; both in the safe order, released = 1.0 (success when this holds for 1 s with the leads at rest).
reset_notes: Take both clamps out of the pads and lay each lead straight on the table along its tape line (red y 6, black y 0) with the clamp lying flat, its far end at x 15.4 cm. The lead ends at the donor battery stay clamped to the table; check the battery and engine blocks sit on their outlines.
fidelity: Leads are 19 rigid 2 cm segments with bending springs, no twist, no plasticity; each clamp is a rigid box welded to the lead end (a real clamp's jaws are not modelled: seated in the recess stands for clamped on the post). Lead ends are fixed to the table at the donor battery. Batteries, engine block and pads are fixed rigid boxes; no electricity is simulated: the order and contact rules stand in for spark and short-circuit risk.
